sentences.text: Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties resided separately from 12.04.2019.

Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged a complaint against petitioner no. 1 (husband), petitioner no. 2 (father-in-law, since deceased), petitioner no. 3 (mother-in-law), petitioner no. 4 (brother-in-law), petitioner no. 5 (sister-in-law), petitioner no. 6 (sister-in-law), petitioner no. 7 (sister- in-law) and petitioner no. 8 (brother-in-law).

6. On 11.07.2023, parties arrived at a settlement vide a compromise deed dated 11.07.2023 before Counselling Cell, Family Courts, East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi (Annexure P-2) and as per the said settlement, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan, permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Family Courts, East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi

sentences.text: 7. In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by a decree of divorce dated 13.10.2023, passed by Shri Manish Khurana, Judge, Family Court, East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi (Annexure P-3).

entities.text: Family Court, East, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Further, as per the settlement, an amount of Rs. 3,50,000/- has already been paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs. 1,50,000/- has been paid to her in Court today, by online transfer into the account of the complainant.
As per the said settlement, custody of the minor child will be with the respondent no. 2 and the petitioner no. 1 will have no visitation rights.
8. Petitioners no.1 to 5 & 7 to 8 and complainant/respondent no. 2 are This is a digitally signed order.

On an oral request made by learned counsel for the petitioner, Petitioner no.6 is exempted from personal appearance as she is stated to be in advance stage of pregnancy.
9. Out of the said settled amount, remaining amount of Rs, 1,50,000/- has been transferred to the account of the complainant online and receipt of the same has been acknowledged by the complainant.
10. The Complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed against the petitioners.
She further states that all the terms of the settlement have been complied with.
11. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
